rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of RegExp in string replacement for command scripts
rawFindings.explanation: The original code uses `new RegExp('%', 'g')` to replace all '%' characters in the command script with the list of ordered packages. The change replaces the regular expression with a plain string '%', which only replaces the first occurrence instead of all occurrences. This changes the intended behavior of replacing all placeholders and can cause incomplete script commands being run.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using a global regular expression for replacement: keep `var placeholder = new RegExp('%', 'g');` and use `mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], placeholder, orderedPackages.join(' '));` to replace all '%' occurrences correctly.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect use of global regexp in script placeholder replacement
rawFindings.explanation: The patch changes the placeholder replacement in the 'hook' function from replacing all occurrences of '%' by orderedPackages joined by space, to replacing only the first occurrence (using a string '%' instead of a RegExp with 'g' flag). This means if the script contains multiple '%' placeholders, only the first one will be replaced, likely breaking scripts that expect all '%' to be substituted.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the use of a global regular expression (e.g. new RegExp('%', 'g')) in line 87 to replace all '%' placeholders in the script string to maintain expected behavior.
